Russian Mining Technology Firm Debuts Advanced Ore Sorting System

A major Russian supplier to the metals and mining sector, Novatek Metallequipment, announced Monday the launch of a new high-capacity ore sorting system designed to increase efficiency in mineral processing plants. The product, named the Sortex-800, was unveiled at the Metallurgy Progress Expo in Yekaterinburg, drawing the attention of industry executives and technology partners from across the region.

According to Novatek Metallequipment, the Sortex-800 utilizes an array of precision sensors and AI-driven algorithms to detect and separate valuable minerals from raw ore at speeds up to 800 tons per hour. The company claims the system can boost ore recovery rates by up to 15% while reducing energy consumption compared to conventional sorting lines.

"Our new platform is the result of three years of research and pilot projects with leading Russian mining companies," said Sergei Belov, Novatek Metallequipment's chief executive officer. "We believe Sortex-800 will help our clients increase yields, lower costs, and improve their environmental performance."

The launch comes as Russian mining firms seek to modernize operations and improve resource efficiency amid volatile global commodity prices. According to the Russian Association of Metallurgy and Mining, the domestic sector invested over 32 billion rubles in equipment upgrades last year, with a growing share allocated to automation and digitalization technologies.

Industry analysts welcomed the introduction of the Sortex-800, noting the potential for increased competitiveness. "Russian mining is under pressure to optimize extraction as ore grades decline in mature deposits," said Natalia Koroleva, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Mining Institute. "Advanced sorting systems like this can deliver clear economic and environmental benefits by reducing waste and lowering processing costs."

The system will be produced at Novatek Metallequipment's facility in Sverdlovsk region, with initial deliveries scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2024. The company reports that it has signed agreements to pilot the system at three major mining sites in the Urals and Siberia, covering copper, iron ore, and polymetallic operations.

Trade union representatives present at the launch expressed cautious optimism, emphasizing the importance of workforce training as new technologies are implemented. "Innovation is positive, but we must ensure that workers are prepared to operate and maintain this new generation of equipment," said Anton Sidorov, regional chairman of the Mining and Metallurgical Workers Union.

Novatek Metallequipment expects to expand its customer base in Central Asia and Eastern Europe, capitalizing on growing demand for advanced mineral processing solutions. Company officials indicated further software upgrades for the Sortex platform are already in development.
